quote.quote: The benefit-risk of avacopan for the treatment of adult patients with AAV (GPA and MPA) was discussed at an Arthritis Advisory Committee meeting on May 6, 2021, that included relevant rheumatology, nephrology, statistical, and clinical pharmacology experts.

The benefit-risk of avacopan for the treatment of adult patients with AAV (GPA and MPA) was discussed at an Arthritis Advisory Committee meeting on May 6, 2021, that included relevant rheumatology, nephrology, statistical, and clinical pharmacology experts.

recommendation.text: The committee was split. Efficacy vote: 9 Yes / 9 No; Safety vote: 10 Yes / 8 No; Benefit-risk vote: 10 Yes / 8 No. There was no clear majority recommendation for or against approval.

quote.quote: The Committee members were generally split as to whether the application included sufficient efficacy or safety data to support approval and whether the benefit-risk profile sufficiently supported the use of avacopan for the treatment of AAV.

linkages.concern: The committee members who voted 'No' on efficacy said a single trial did not provide enough evidence to support the broad proposed indication for AAV.
linkages.change: The proposed indication was narrowed: avacopan was approved as an adjunctive treatment (in combination with standard therapy including glucocorticoids) for adult patients with severe active AAV, rather than the broad originally-proposed indication.

concern_quote.quote: The committee members who voted "No" agreed that there is not enough substantial clinical and statistical evidence from a single trial to support approval of avacopan for the proposed broad indication.

change_quote.quote: In the Clinical Information Amendment (dated June 18, 2021), the Applicant revised the proposed indication in accordance with the Advisory Committee meeting and discussions with the Agency.

linkages.concern: The committee was divided on whether the data supported avacopan as a steroid-sparing agent; members noted avacopan may not eliminate the use of steroids.
linkages.change: The approved indication explicitly states that avacopan is used in combination with standard therapy including glucocorticoids and 'does not eliminate glucocorticoid use.'

concern_quote.quote: the committee noted that avacopan may not eliminate the use of steroids, but some members felt the data support decreased steroid use with avacopan treatment, while others stated differences in GC use observed in the first half of the study were a result of the nature of the design and questioned the clinical relevance of the observed differences.

change_quote.quote: in combination with standard therapy including glucocorticoids. [Tradename] does not eliminate glucocorticoid use.

linkages.concern: Committee members stated a need for confirmatory evidence from another study and recommended a study designed to evaluate the drug (e.g., as maintenance therapy).
linkages.change: A postmarketing requirement (PMR) study was agreed upon to provide additional comparative safety and efficacy data; the review team ties the AAC input to the conclusion that the narrowed indication plus the postmarketing study would mitigate uncertainties.

concern_quote.quote: Some committee members stated the need for confirmatory evidence from another study, and some suggested that the drug may be better positioned as a maintenance therapy and recommended a study designed to evaluate this.

change_quote.quote: The review team further notes the input provided by the Medical Policy and Program Review Council and the Arthritis Advisory Committee, and the divided recommendations offered by each.

linkages.concern: Committee members who voted 'No' on safety raised concerns including a short-term safety database and the risks of angioedema and hepatotoxicity.
linkages.change: The Agency added hepatotoxicity safety controls to labeling: a limitation of use so avacopan would not be recommended for patients with active/uncontrolled chronic liver disease and cirrhosis, placed under Section 5 (Warnings and Precautions).

concern_quote.quote: The committee members who voted “No” expressed concerns with the following: 1) small sample size; 2) shorter term safety database (as compared to knowledge of long-term safety of steroids); 3) risks of angioedema and hepatotoxicity; and 4) lack of data in minority groups.

change_quote.quote: Due to safety concerns for hepatotoxicity, a limitation of use was considered so that avacopan would not be recommended for patients with active, untreated and/or uncontrolled chronic liver disease (e.g., chronic active hepatitis B, untreated hepatitis C, uncontrolled autoimmune hepatitis) and cirrhosis.

summary: The Arthritis Advisory Committee met on May 6, 2021 for NDA 214487 (avacopan/TAVNEOS) and split closely on efficacy (9-9), safety (10-8), and benefit-risk (10-8), with no clear majority recommendation. Following the meeting and subsequent Agency-Applicant discussions, the originally broad indication was narrowed to adjunctive treatment of adult patients with severe active AAV in combination with standard therapy including glucocorticoids, with explicit language that avacopan 'does not eliminate glucocorticoid use,' and a postmarketing requirement study was agreed upon to address the confirmatory-evidence and safety concerns raised. Hepatotoxicity concerns raised by dissenting members are reflected in labeling limitations, though the review does not explicitly connect that AAC concern to the specific labeling change.
